questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Breathing: respiratory organs and the human respiratory system
questions.question: Which structure covers the glottis during swallowing and so prevents food from entering the larynx?

solution.key_concept: The epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that closes the glottis during swallowing.
steps: The pharynx is the common passage for food and air.
During swallowing, the epiglottis covers the glottis, so food is directed away from the larynx.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Epiglottis
solution.why_not_others: The larynx is the cartilaginous sound box. The pleura covers the lungs. The diaphragm forms the floor of the thoracic chamber.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the larynx (the sound box) with the epiglottis (the flap that guards the glottis).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Breathing: respiratory organs and the human respiratory system
questions.question: At the level of which vertebra does the human trachea divide into the right and left primary bronchi?

solution.key_concept: The trachea bifurcates into the two primary bronchi at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra.
steps: The trachea runs down through the thoracic cavity.
It divides into the right and left primary bronchi at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): 5th thoracic vertebra
solution.why_not_others: The 3rd thoracic and 7th cervical vertebrae lie too high. The lumbar vertebrae lie below the thorax.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the vertebra number or the vertebral region.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember: bifurcation at T5.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Breathing: respiratory organs and the human respiratory system
questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the respiratory or exchange part of the human respiratory system?

solution.key_concept: The conducting part runs from the nostrils to the terminal bronchioles. The alveoli and their ducts form the exchange part.
steps: The trachea, the bronchi and the terminal bronchioles only conduct air.
The alveoli and alveolar ducts form the respiratory or exchange part.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Alveolar ducts
solution.why_not_others: Terminal bronchioles are the last segment of the conducting part. The tertiary bronchi and trachea are also conducting structures.
solution.common_trap: Assuming the terminal bronchioles take part in gas exchange because they are the last branches before the alveoli.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Breathing: respiratory organs and the human respiratory system
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Human lungs are situated in an air-tight thoracic chamber.
statements.R: The pleural fluid between the two layers of pleura reduces friction on the lung surface.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: The air-tight thorax and the pleural fluid are separate features of lung anatomy.
steps: A is true: the lungs lie in an air-tight thoracic chamber.
R is true: the pleural fluid reduces friction.
Reducing friction does not explain why the chamber is air-tight, so R does not explain A.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are factually correct, so options 3 and 4 are ruled out. R is unrelated to the air-tightness described in A, so option 1 is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Linking any two true pleura or thorax facts as cause and effect.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Breathing: respiratory organs and the human respiratory system
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The trachea, the primary, secondary and tertiary bronchi and the initial bronchioles are supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings.
statements.II: The conducting part of the respiratory system extends from the external nostrils to the alveolar ducts and is the site of gas exchange.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Cartilaginous support of the airways, and the boundary between the conducting and exchange parts.
steps: Statement I is correct: these airways are supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings.
The conducting part ends at the terminal bronchioles.
The conducting part only filters, humidifies and warms air, and does not exchange gases.
So Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II misplaces the end of the conducting part and gives it an exchange role.
solution.common_trap: Including the alveolar ducts in the conducting part.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of breathing and its regulation
questions.question: On average, a healthy human breathes how many times per minute?

solution.key_concept: The normal breathing rate of a healthy human is 12-16 per minute.
steps: A healthy human breathes 12 to 16 times per minute.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): 12-16
solution.why_not_others: 6-8 is too low and 20-25 is too high. 70-75 is the heart rate.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the breathing rate with the heart beat rate.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of breathing and its regulation
questions.question: Which centre moderates the respiratory rhythm by reducing the duration of inspiration and altering the respiratory rate?
options: Respiratory rhythm centre in the medulla
Chemosensitive area adjacent to the rhythm centre

solution.key_concept: The pneumotaxic centre in the pons moderates the rhythm set by the medullary centre.
steps: The medullary rhythm centre sets the basic rhythm.
The pneumotaxic centre in the pons shortens inspiration and alters the rate.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Pneumotaxic centre in the pons
solution.why_not_others: The rhythm centre sets the rhythm but does not moderate it. The chemosensitive area and the aortic arch receptors sense $CO_2$ and $H^+$.
solution.common_trap: Placing the pneumotaxic centre in the medulla, or confusing it with the rhythm centre.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of breathing and its regulation
questions.question: A healthy person has a tidal volume of 500 mL and breathes 14 times per minute. What is the volume of air inspired per minute?

solution.key_concept: Minute ventilation is tidal volume multiplied by the breathing rate.
steps: Use $V_{min} = TV \times f$.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): 7000 mL
solution.why_not_others: 514 mL comes from adding instead of multiplying. 3500 mL comes from halving the rate. 6000 mL uses a rate of 12 instead of 14.
solution.common_trap: Using the textbook rate of 12 instead of the rate given in the question.
solution.time_saving_tip: Calculate $5 \times 14 = 70$, then multiply by 100.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of breathing and its regulation
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Increase in thoracic volume in the antero-posterior axis

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Increase in thoracic volume in the dorso-ventral axis

solution.key_concept: Each inspiratory muscle enlarges the thorax along a specific axis, and each regulatory centre has a specific location and role.
steps: The diaphragm enlarges the thorax in the antero-posterior axis: A-I.
The external intercostals lift the ribs and sternum, enlarging the dorso-ventral axis: B-II.
The pneumotaxic centre lies in the pons: C-III.
The chemosensitive area senses $CO_2$ and $H^+$: D-IV.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap the two axes, or swap the functions of the two centres.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the antero-posterior and dorso-ventral axes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of breathing and its regulation
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the mechanism and regulation of breathing are correct?

statements.A: Normal expiration is passive and occurs by relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles.
statements.B: During inspiration the intra-pulmonary pressure becomes higher than the atmospheric pressure.
statements.C: Receptors in the aortic arch and carotid artery can recognise changes in $CO_2$ and $H^+$ concentration.
statements.D: Oxygen plays a major role in the regulation of the respiratory rhythm.
statements.E: Abdominal muscles can increase the strength of breathing.

solution.key_concept: Pressure changes during the breathing cycle, and the chemical regulation of breathing.
steps: A is true: normal expiration is passive.
B is false: during inspiration the intra-pulmonary pressure falls below atmospheric pressure.
C is true: the aortic arch and carotid receptors detect $CO_2$ and $H^+$.
D is false: oxygen has an insignificant role in regulation.
E is true: abdominal muscles can add force to breathing.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 3 and 4 include the false statements B and/or D. Option 1 omits the true statement E.
solution.common_trap: Assuming oxygen is the main chemical regulator of breathing.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Exchange and transport of gases; respiratory volumes
questions.question: What percentage of oxygen is transported by RBCs in the blood as oxyhaemoglobin?

solution.key_concept: Most of the $O_2$ in blood is carried bound to haemoglobin.
steps: About 97% of $O_2$ travels as oxyhaemoglobin in RBCs.
The remaining 3% is dissolved in plasma.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): About 97%
solution.why_not_others: 3% is the dissolved fraction of $O_2$. 7% and 70% are the dissolved and bicarbonate fractions of $CO_2$.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the $O_2$ transport percentages with the $CO_2$ transport percentages.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Exchange and transport of gases; respiratory volumes
questions.question: A person has TV = 500 mL, IRV = 2500 mL, ERV = 1000 mL and RV = 1200 mL. What is the vital capacity?

solution.key_concept: Vital capacity is the sum of IRV, TV and ERV.
steps: Use $VC = IRV + TV + ERV$.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): 4000 mL
solution.why_not_others: 3000 mL is the inspiratory capacity (TV + IRV). 5200 mL is the total lung capacity (VC + RV). 2200 mL is the functional residual capacity (ERV + RV).
solution.common_trap: Adding the residual volume into the vital capacity.
solution.time_saving_tip: RV is never part of VC, because RV can never be expelled.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Exchange and transport of gases; respiratory volumes
questions.question: Which set of conditions favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin?
options: High $pO_2$, low $pCO_2$, low $H^+$ and lower temperature
Low $pO_2$, high $pCO_2$, high $H^+$ and higher temperature
High $pO_2$, high $pCO_2$, high $H^+$ and higher temperature
Low $pO_2$, low $pCO_2$, low $H^+$ and lower temperature

solution.key_concept: Conditions in the alveoli favour the binding of $O_2$ to haemoglobin.
steps: The alveoli have high $pO_2$, low $pCO_2$, low $H^+$ and lower temperature.
These conditions favour oxyhaemoglobin formation.
The reverse conditions, found in the tissues, favour dissociation.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): High $pO_2$, low $pCO_2$, low $H^+$ and lower temperature
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 describes tissue conditions, which favour dissociation. Options 3 and 4 mix favourable and unfavourable factors.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that higher temperature or higher $H^+$ helps $O_2$ binding.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Exchange and transport of gases; respiratory volumes
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: For the same difference in partial pressure, $CO_2$ diffuses across the alveolar membrane much more readily than $O_2$.
statements.R: The solubility of $CO_2$ is 20 to 25 times higher than that of $O_2$.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: The rate of diffusion depends on the solubility of the gas.
steps: Diffusion depends on the pressure gradient, the solubility of the gas and the membrane thickness.
$CO_2$ is 20 to 25 times more soluble than $O_2$.
Its higher solubility explains why it diffuses more readily per unit pressure difference.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, so options 3 and 4 are wrong. Solubility directly explains the diffusion difference, so option 2 is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that $CO_2$ diffuses poorly because its partial pressure gradient is small.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Exchange and transport of gases; respiratory volumes
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The $pO_2$ of alveolar air (104 mm Hg) is higher than that of deoxygenated blood (40 mm Hg), so $O_2$ diffuses from the alveoli into the blood.
statements.II: About 70% of $CO_2$ is transported as bicarbonate, whose formation is catalysed by carbonic anhydrase.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Partial pressure gradients drive diffusion, and $CO_2$ is carried mainly as bicarbonate.
steps: The alveolar $pO_2$ is 104 mm Hg and the deoxygenated blood $pO_2$ is 40 mm Hg, so $O_2$ moves into the blood. Statement I is correct.
About 70% of $CO_2$ is carried as bicarbonate, formed with the help of carbonic anhydrase. Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the stated values and mechanisms.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the 70% bicarbonate share with the 20-25% carbamino-haemoglobin share.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Respiratory disorders: asthma, emphysema, occupational disorders
questions.question: Emphysema is characterised by:
options: Damage to alveolar walls, which decreases the respiratory surface
Inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles, which causes wheezing
Fibrosis caused by inhaling silica dust
Proliferation of fibrous tissue caused by asbestos fibres

solution.key_concept: Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which the alveolar walls are damaged.
steps: In emphysema the alveolar walls are damaged.
As a result, the respiratory surface area decreases.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Damage to alveolar walls, which decreases the respiratory surface
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 describes asthma. Option 3 describes silicosis. Option 4 describes asbestosis.
solution.common_trap: Confusing emphysema with asthma.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Respiratory disorders: asthma, emphysema, occupational disorders
questions.question: Difficulty in breathing with wheezing, caused by inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles, is characteristic of:

solution.key_concept: Asthma is caused by inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles.
steps: Wheezing together with inflamed bronchi and bronchioles indicates asthma.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Asthma
solution.why_not_others: Emphysema involves damage to the alveolar walls. Silicosis and asbestosis are occupational fibrotic disorders caused by dust.
solution.common_trap: Choosing emphysema just because it is also a chronic breathing difficulty.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Respiratory disorders: asthma, emphysema, occupational disorders
questions.question: Long exposure to dust in stone-breaking industries causes inflammation of the lungs. This inflammation leads to:

solution.key_concept: In occupational disorders, dust causes inflammation, which then leads to fibrosis.
steps: The dust overwhelms the body's defence mechanisms.
Long exposure causes inflammation, which leads to fibrosis (proliferation of fibrous tissue).
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Fibrosis
solution.why_not_others: Dust damage does not dilate the bronchioles or increase the alveolar surface. Thinning of the pleura is not a stated outcome.
solution.common_trap: Assuming the lung tissue thins out, when in fact fibrous tissue proliferates.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Respiratory disorders: asthma, emphysema, occupational disorders
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Each respiratory disorder has a characteristic cause or lesion.
steps: Asthma: inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles, so A-II.
Emphysema: damaged alveolar walls, so B-IV.
Silicosis: silica dust, so C-III.
Asbestosis: asbestos fibres, so D-I.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap asthma with emphysema, and/or swap silica with asbestos.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the lesions of asthma and emphysema.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Respiratory disorders: asthma, emphysema, occupational disorders
questions.question: Which of the following statements about respiratory disorders are correct?

statements.A: Asthma results from damage to the alveolar walls.
statements.B: Emphysema is a chronic disorder in which the respiratory surface decreases.
statements.C: Occupational respiratory disorders arise when the dust produced is so great that the body's defence mechanisms cannot cope.
statements.D: Fibrosis refers to the proliferation of fibrous tissue.
statements.E: Protective masks are of no value in preventing occupational respiratory disorders.

solution.key_concept: The features and prevention of asthma, emphysema and occupational disorders.
steps: A is false: asthma is inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles.
B is true: in emphysema the respiratory surface decreases.
C is true: occupational disorders arise when dust exceeds the body's defences.
D is true: fibrosis is the proliferation of fibrous tissue.
E is false: workers should wear protective masks.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): B, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 3 each include the false statement A and/or E.
solution.common_trap: Attributing alveolar damage to asthma instead of emphysema.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Blood composition, blood groups and coagulation
questions.question: Which plasma protein is mainly responsible for maintaining the osmotic balance of blood?

solution.key_concept: Each major plasma protein has a distinct role: fibrinogen in clotting, globulins in defence and albumins in osmotic balance.
steps: Recall the three main plasma proteins and their roles.
Fibrinogen is needed for clotting, and globulins are needed for defence.
Albumins maintain osmotic balance.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Albumin
solution.why_not_others: Fibrinogen is needed for coagulation. Globulins function in defence. Prothrombin is converted into thrombin during clotting.
solution.common_trap: Picking globulin because it is also a major plasma protein, even though its role is defence.
solution.time_saving_tip: Link the first letters: Albumin goes with osmotic balance, Fibrinogen with clotting, Globulin with defence.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Blood composition, blood groups and coagulation
questions.question: A person's plasma contains anti-A antibodies but no anti-B antibodies. The blood group of this person is:

solution.key_concept: In the ABO system, plasma carries antibodies against the antigens that are absent from that person's own RBCs.
steps: Anti-A is present, so antigen A must be absent from the RBCs.
Anti-B is absent, so antigen B must be present on the RBCs.
RBCs that carry only antigen B belong to group B.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): B
solution.why_not_others: Group A has anti-B antibodies. Group AB has no antibodies. Group O has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.
solution.common_trap: Matching the antibody name directly to the blood group and wrongly choosing group A.
solution.time_saving_tip: The antibody is always named after the antigen the person lacks.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Blood composition, blood groups and coagulation
questions.question: Which type of white blood cell forms about 0.5 to 1% of the total WBCs and secretes histamine, serotonin and heparin?

solution.key_concept: The WBC types differ in their percentage of the total count and in their function.
steps: Basophils make up 0.5 to 1% of WBCs.
Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Basophils
solution.why_not_others: Eosinophils make up 2 to 3% and are linked to allergy. Neutrophils make up 60 to 65% and are phagocytic. Monocytes make up 6 to 8% and are phagocytic.
solution.common_trap: Choosing eosinophils because both eosinophils and histamine are associated with allergic reactions.
solution.time_saving_tip: Basophils are the least abundant WBCs, and they are the ones that release histamine and heparin.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Blood composition, blood groups and coagulation
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Removing $Ca^{2+}$ ions from a freshly collected blood sample prevents it from clotting.
statements.R: $Ca^{2+}$ ions are essential for the coagulation of blood, including the conversion of prothrombin into thrombin.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Thrombokinase converts prothrombin into thrombin, and this step requires $Ca^{2+}$ ions.
steps: Thrombokinase converts prothrombin into thrombin only in the presence of $Ca^{2+}$.
Without thrombin, soluble fibrinogen cannot be converted into insoluble fibrin.
So removing $Ca^{2+}$ stops clot formation, and R directly explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are factually correct. R gives the exact reason why A happens, so the options saying one statement is false, or that R does not explain A, are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that $Ca^{2+}$ only affects a minor step, and therefore marking R as not explaining A.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Blood composition, blood groups and coagulation
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur during the second pregnancy of an Rh-negative mother who is carrying an Rh-positive foetus.
statements.II: Erythroblastosis foetalis is prevented by giving anti-Rh antibodies to the Rh-negative mother at the end of her second pregnancy.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Rh incompatibility affects a later pregnancy, so preventive treatment must be given right after the first delivery.
steps: Statement I correctly describes the condition in which erythroblastosis foetalis can occur.
Prevention requires giving anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the first delivery.
Giving them at the end of the second pregnancy is too late, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement I matches the notes exactly. Statement II gives the wrong timing for the antibody injection, so no option that marks it correct can be right.
solution.common_trap: Reading only 'anti-Rh antibodies to the mother' and missing the incorrect timing.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember: treat the mother right after the first delivery.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lymph: composition and function
questions.question: Lymph is a colourless fluid because it lacks:

solution.key_concept: The colour of blood comes from its RBCs, which are absent from lymph.
steps: Most formed elements, including RBCs, stay inside the blood vessels.
Lymph therefore has no RBCs, which makes it colourless.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): RBCs
solution.why_not_others: Lymph contains lymphocytes. It has fewer proteins than plasma but is not completely free of them. Lymph is mostly water.
solution.common_trap: Choosing plasma proteins because lymph has fewer proteins than plasma.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lymph: composition and function
questions.question: After digestion, fats absorbed in the small intestine first enter the:
options: Blood capillaries of the intestinal villi

solution.key_concept: Fats are absorbed through lymph rather than directly into blood.
steps: Each intestinal villus contains a lymph vessel called a lacteal.
Fats are absorbed into the lymph present in these lacteals.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Lacteals in the intestinal villi
solution.why_not_others: Blood capillaries and the hepatic portal vein are not the entry route for fats. The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs and plays no part in absorption.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that all digested nutrients enter the blood capillaries.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lymph: composition and function
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the formation of interstitial (tissue) fluid?
options: Water and small water-soluble substances leave the capillaries, while larger proteins and most formed elements remain in the vessels
Larger proteins and RBCs leave the capillaries, while water remains in the vessels
All plasma components and formed elements leave the capillaries in equal proportion
Only respiratory gases leave the capillaries, while water and solutes remain in the vessels

solution.key_concept: Tissue fluid forms when capillaries let out water and small solutes but hold back large molecules and cells.
steps: As blood passes through capillaries, water and small water-soluble substances move out into the spaces between cells.
Larger proteins and most formed elements stay inside the vessels.
This fluid in the spaces between cells is called interstitial fluid.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Water and small water-soluble substances leave the capillaries, while larger proteins and most formed elements remain in the vessels
solution.why_not_others: Large proteins and RBCs are held back, not released. Leakage is selective, not equal for all components. Water and small solutes do leave the capillaries, not just gases.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that tissue fluid has the same composition as whole blood.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lymph: composition and function
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Absorb fats in the intestinal villi

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Mineral distribution similar to that of plasma

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Drain lymph back into the major veins

solution.key_concept: Each component of the lymphatic system has a specific feature or role.
steps: Interstitial fluid has a mineral distribution similar to plasma, so A matches II.
Lacteals absorb fats in the villi, so B matches I.
Lymphocytes are responsible for immune responses, so C matches III.
Lymphatic vessels drain lymph into the major veins, so D matches IV.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 swaps A and B. Option 3 wrongly links lacteals with immunity. Option 4 wrongly links interstitial fluid with drainage into the veins.
solution.common_trap: Confusing interstitial fluid with the lymphatic vessels that collect it.
solution.time_saving_tip: B-I is certain from the fats clue alone, which leaves only options 1 and 4. Then A-II settles the answer.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lymph: composition and function
questions.question: Which of the following statements about lymph are correct?

statements.A: Lymph contains more proteins than plasma.
statements.B: Lymph is an important carrier of nutrients and hormones.
statements.C: Lymph returns tissue fluid to the major veins.
statements.D: Interstitial fluid contains most of the formed elements of blood.
statements.E: Lymph contains specialised lymphocytes responsible for immune responses.

solution.key_concept: Lymph is derived from tissue fluid. It is poor in proteins, lacks most formed elements, and has transport and immune roles.
steps: A is false because lymph has fewer proteins than plasma.
B and C are true.
D is false because most formed elements stay inside the vessels.
E is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): B, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 4 include a false statement (A in option 1; A and D in option 4). Option 2 leaves out the true statement E.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting that lymph contains lymphocytes even though it lacks RBCs.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human heart and blood vessels
questions.question: In the human heart, the AV node is located in the:
options: Lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrioventricular septum
Right upper corner of the right atrium
Upper corner of the left atrium
Base of the interventricular septum within the left ventricle

solution.key_concept: Both the SA node and the AV node lie in the right atrium, but at different positions.
steps: The SA node lies in the right upper corner of the right atrium.
The AV node lies in the lower left corner of the right atrium, near the AV septum.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrioventricular septum
solution.why_not_others: The right upper corner of the right atrium is the site of the SA node. Neither node lies in the left atrium or in the left ventricle.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the position of the AV node with that of the SA node.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human heart and blood vessels
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists only of animals that have a four-chambered heart?

solution.key_concept: The number of heart chambers differs among vertebrate groups.
steps: Fishes have a 2-chambered heart.
Amphibians and most reptiles have a 3-chambered heart.
Crocodiles, birds and mammals have a 4-chambered heart.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Crocodiles, birds and mammals
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 3 include fishes, which have two chambers. Options 1 and 2 include amphibians, which have three chambers. Option 2 also includes most reptiles, which have three chambers.
solution.common_trap: Grouping crocodiles with other reptiles as having a 3-chambered heart.
solution.time_saving_tip: Eliminate any option that contains fishes or amphibians.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human heart and blood vessels
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: The pulmonary artery carries oxygenated blood.
statements.R: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Arteries are defined by the direction of blood flow, not by how much oxygen the blood carries.
steps: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs, so A is false.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so the options that treat A as true (1, 2 and 3) are ruled out. R is a correct general fact, which leaves option 4.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that all arteries carry oxygenated blood.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human heart and blood vessels
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Capillary walls consist of three layers: tunica intima, tunica media and tunica externa.
statements.II: Veins have thicker walls than arteries and lack valves.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: The structure of a vessel's wall suits its function.
steps: Capillary walls are one cell thick and consist of endothelium only, so Statement I is incorrect.
The three tunics are found in the walls of arteries and veins.
Veins have thinner walls than arteries and do have valves, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains a factual error, so no option that marks either statement correct is valid.
solution.common_trap: Applying the three-layered wall structure of arteries and veins to capillaries.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cardiac cycle, cardiac output and ECG
questions.question: The second heart sound 'dub' is produced by the:
options: Closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves

solution.key_concept: Heart sounds are produced when the heart valves close.
steps: When the AV valves close at the start of ventricular systole, the first sound 'lub' is produced.
When the semilunar valves close as the ventricles relax, the second sound 'dub' is produced.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Closure of the semilunar valves
solution.why_not_others: Closure of the AV valves produces 'lub'. The opening of valves and the contraction of the atria are not the cause of 'dub'.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the causes of 'lub' and 'dub'.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cardiac cycle, cardiac output and ECG
questions.question: An athlete has a stroke volume of 80 mL and a heart rate of 75 beats per minute. What is the athlete's cardiac output?

solution.key_concept: Cardiac output is calculated as $CO = SV \times HR$.
steps: Substitute the values: $CO = 80\,mL \times 75 = 6000\,mL/min$.
Convert to litres: $6000\,mL = 6.0\,L$, so the cardiac output is 6.0 L per minute.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): 6.0 L per minute
solution.why_not_others: 0.6 L and 60 L both come from errors in converting mL to L. 5.0 L is the typical value for a resting adult, not the value calculated from the given data.
solution.common_trap: Recalling the textbook value of 5 L/min instead of calculating from the data given.
solution.time_saving_tip: Since $8 \times 75 = 600$, it follows that $80 \times 75 = 6000$.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cardiac cycle, cardiac output and ECG
questions.question: In a normal ECG, the end of the T wave marks the:

solution.key_concept: Each wave of the ECG corresponds to a specific electrical event in the heart.
steps: The T wave represents ventricular repolarisation.
The end of the T wave marks the end of systole.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): End of ventricular systole
solution.why_not_others: The P wave reflects atrial depolarisation, which leads to atrial contraction. The QRS complex marks the onset of ventricular depolarisation.
solution.common_trap: Linking the T wave with depolarisation rather than repolarisation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cardiac cycle, cardiac output and ECG
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: All chambers relaxed with the AV valves open

solution.key_concept: ECG waves and the phases of the cardiac cycle each correspond to specific events.
steps: The P wave represents atrial depolarisation, so A matches III.
The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarisation, so B matches IV.
The T wave represents ventricular repolarisation, so C matches I.
In joint diastole all chambers are relaxed and the AV valves are open, so D matches II.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the events of the P wave and the QRS complex. Option 2 swaps the events of the QRS complex and the T wave. Option 4 swaps the matches for the P wave and joint diastole.
solution.common_trap: Confusing ventricular depolarisation with ventricular repolarisation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cardiac cycle, cardiac output and ECG
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the cardiac cycle are correct?

statements.A: At a heart rate of 72 beats per minute, one cardiac cycle lasts about 0.8 s.
statements.B: Atrial systole increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30%.
statements.C: The semilunar valves remain open during joint diastole.
statements.D: The first heart sound is caused by the closure of the AV valves.
statements.E: Non-athletes have a higher cardiac output than athletes.

solution.key_concept: This question tests the timing, valve events and output of the cardiac cycle.
steps: A is true because $60/72 \approx 0.8\,s$.
B is true.
C is false because the semilunar valves are closed during joint diastole.
D is true.
E is false because athletes have a higher cardiac output than non-athletes.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 4 include the false statement C. Option 3 includes the false statement E and leaves out the true statement A.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that all valves are open during joint diastole.
solution.time_saving_tip: C is false, which rules out options 1 and 4. E is false, which rules out option 3.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Double circulation and regulation of cardiac activity
questions.question: Which chamber of the human heart pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery?

solution.key_concept: Pulmonary circulation begins at the right ventricle.
steps: In pulmonary circulation, the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs.
The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta, not the pulmonary artery.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Right ventricle
solution.why_not_others: The left ventricle pumps into the aorta. The atria receive blood and do not pump into the pulmonary artery. The right atrium receives blood from the venae cavae and the left atrium receives blood from the pulmonary veins.
solution.common_trap: Assuming arteries always carry oxygenated blood. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood.
solution.time_saving_tip: Right side means deoxygenated blood going to the lungs.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Double circulation and regulation of cardiac activity
questions.question: In double circulation, oxygenated blood returning from the lungs first enters which chamber of the heart, and through which vessels?
options: Right atrium, through the pulmonary veins
Left atrium, through the pulmonary veins
Left atrium, through the pulmonary artery
Left ventricle, through the venae cavae

solution.key_concept: Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood to the left atrium.
steps: The pulmonary circuit runs from the right ventricle to the lungs and then to the left atrium.
The vessels carrying blood from the lungs to the heart are the pulmonary veins.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Left atrium, through the pulmonary veins
solution.why_not_others: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the venae cavae. The pulmonary artery carries blood away from the heart to the lungs. The venae cavae drain the body, not the lungs.
solution.common_trap: Thinking veins always carry deoxygenated blood. The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Double circulation and regulation of cardiac activity
questions.question: Stimulation of the parasympathetic nerves supplying the human heart results in:
options: Decrease in heart rate, speed of conduction and cardiac output
Increase in heart rate and strength of ventricular contraction
Decrease in heart rate but increase in cardiac output
Complete stoppage of the heartbeat, because the heart is neurogenic

solution.key_concept: The parasympathetic nervous system slows the heart.
steps: The cardiac centre in the medulla oblongata moderates heart activity through the ANS.
Parasympathetic nerves decrease heart rate, the speed of conduction and cardiac output.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Decrease in heart rate, speed of conduction and cardiac output
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) describes sympathetic stimulation. Option (3) is wrong because cardiac output also falls. Option (4) is wrong because the human heart is myogenic and only moderated by nerves.
solution.common_trap: Confusing sympathetic effects with parasympathetic effects.
solution.time_saving_tip: Parasympathetic means 'rest': everything in the heart slows down.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Double circulation and regulation of cardiac activity
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: The human heart is described as myogenic.
statements.R: The rhythmic activity of the human heart is initiated by the cardiac centre in the medulla oblongata.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Heart activity is auto-regulated by nodal tissue, and the medulla only moderates it.
steps: Heart activity is auto-regulated by nodal tissue, so the heart is myogenic. A is true.
The medullary cardiac centre only moderates this activity through the ANS and does not initiate it. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options (1) and (2) are wrong. A is true, so option (4) is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Treating neural moderation as if it were initiation of the heartbeat.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Double circulation and regulation of cardiac activity
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In systemic circulation, deoxygenated blood from the tissues returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium.
statements.II: Sympathetic stimulation increases heart rate but decreases the strength of ventricular contraction.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: The venae cavae drain into the right atrium, and sympathetic nerves increase every measure of cardiac activity.
steps: Deoxygenated blood from the tissues returns through the veins and venae cavae to the right atrium. Statement I is incorrect.
Sympathetic nerves increase heart rate, the strength of ventricular contraction and cardiac output. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains a factual error, so no option that calls either statement correct can be right.
solution.common_trap: Partial-truth statements: the first half of Statement II is correct, but its second half is wrong.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Circulatory disorders: hypertension, coronary artery disease, angina pectoris, heart failure
questions.question: Repeated blood pressure readings at or above which value indicate hypertension?

solution.key_concept: Hypertension threshold
steps: Normal blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg (systolic/diastolic).
Repeated readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher indicate hypertension.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): 140/90 mm Hg
solution.why_not_others: 120/80 mm Hg is normal. 130/85 mm Hg is not the stated threshold. 90/140 mm Hg reverses systolic and diastolic values.
solution.common_trap: Reversing systolic and diastolic values.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Circulatory disorders: hypertension, coronary artery disease, angina pectoris, heart failure
questions.question: Heart failure is also called congestive heart failure because:
options: Heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply
Coronary arteries become congested with cholesterol deposits
Congestion of the lungs is one of its main symptoms

solution.key_concept: Heart failure and the reason for its alternative name
steps: Heart failure is the state in which the heart cannot pump blood effectively enough to meet the body's needs.
It is called congestive heart failure because congestion of the lungs is a main symptom.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Congestion of the lungs is one of its main symptoms
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) describes cardiac arrest. Option (2) describes a heart attack. Option (3) describes coronary artery disease.
solution.common_trap: Equating heart failure with cardiac arrest or a heart attack.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Circulatory disorders: hypertension, coronary artery disease, angina pectoris, heart failure
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Sudden damage to heart muscle due to inadequate blood supply

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Repeated blood pressure readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Narrowing of the lumen of vessels supplying the heart muscle by deposits

solution.key_concept: Distinguishing the circulatory disorders
steps: Hypertension is a blood pressure of 140/90 mm Hg or above (A-III).
In CAD, deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue narrow the coronary vessels (B-IV).
In cardiac arrest the heart stops beating (C-I), while in a heart attack heart muscle is suddenly damaged (D-II).
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps cardiac arrest and heart attack. Option (2) swaps hypertension and CAD. Option (3) mismatches hypertension and cardiac arrest.
solution.common_trap: Treating cardiac arrest and heart attack as the same condition.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Circulatory disorders: hypertension, coronary artery disease, angina pectoris, heart failure
questions.question: Which of the following statements about circulatory disorders are correct?

statements.A: Hypertension can affect vital organs such as the brain and kidney.
statements.B: Deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue narrow the vessels in coronary artery disease.
statements.C: Heart failure and cardiac arrest are the same condition.
statements.D: Atherosclerosis mainly affects the pulmonary veins.
statements.E: Angina pectoris can occur in both men and women at any age.

options: A, B, C and E only

solution.key_concept: Facts about hypertension, CAD, angina and heart failure
steps: A is true: hypertension affects the brain and kidney.
B is true: these are the deposits found in CAD.
C is false: in heart failure the heart pumps ineffectively, while in cardiac arrest it stops beating.
D is false: atherosclerosis affects the vessels supplying the heart muscle.
E is true: angina occurs in both sexes at any age.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, B and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) omits E. Option (2) includes the false statement C. Option (3) includes the false statement D and omits A.
solution.common_trap: Accepting C because the two conditions sound similar.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting C and D eliminates options (2) and (3) immediately.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Modes of excretion: ammonotelism, ureotelism and uricotelism
questions.question: Which nitrogenous waste is excreted as a pellet or paste with minimum loss of water?

solution.key_concept: Uricotelism conserves water
steps: Toxicity and water requirement follow the order ammonia > urea > uric acid.
Uricotelic animals excrete uric acid as a pellet or paste with minimum water loss.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Uric acid
solution.why_not_others: Urea needs more water than uric acid. Ammonia, excreted as $NH_4^+$, needs the most water.
solution.common_trap: Thinking urea is the least water-demanding waste.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Modes of excretion: ammonotelism, ureotelism and uricotelism
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists only of ureotelic animals?
options: Mammals, terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes
Bony fishes, aquatic amphibians and aquatic insects

solution.key_concept: Classifying animals by their mode of excretion
steps: Ureotelic animals include mammals, many terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes.
Birds are uricotelic, and bony fishes are ammonotelic.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Mammals, terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) lists ammonotelic animals. Option (3) lists uricotelic animals. Option (4) includes birds, which are uricotelic.
solution.common_trap: Grouping marine fishes with ammonotelic bony fishes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Modes of excretion: ammonotelism, ureotelism and uricotelism
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of an animal and its excretory structure is correct?

solution.key_concept: Excretory structures in different animals
steps: Prawns and other crustaceans have antennal (green) glands.
Earthworms have nephridia, insects such as the cockroach have Malpighian tubules, and flatworms have protonephridia.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Prawn – green glands
solution.why_not_others: Options (2) and (3) swap the excretory structures of the earthworm and the cockroach. Flatworms have flame cells, not antennal glands.
solution.common_trap: Swapping nephridia and Malpighian tubules between the earthworm and the cockroach.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Modes of excretion: ammonotelism, ureotelism and uricotelism
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In ammonotelic animals, the kidneys play no significant role in the elimination of ammonia.
statements.R: Ammonia is the least toxic nitrogenous waste and requires very little water for its elimination.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Ammonotelism
steps: Ammonotelic animals excrete $NH_4^+$ by diffusion across body surfaces or gills, and the kidneys play no significant role. A is true.
Ammonia is the most toxic waste and needs the most water. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options (1), (2) and (4) are all wrong.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the toxicity order of the nitrogenous wastes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Modes of excretion: ammonotelism, ureotelism and uricotelism
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Protonephridia (flame cells) of flatworms function mainly in the elimination of nitrogenous wastes rather than in osmoregulation.
statements.II: Marine fishes are ammonotelic, while terrestrial amphibians are uricotelic.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: The function of protonephridia and the ureotelic groups
steps: Protonephridia function mainly in osmoregulation. Statement I is incorrect.
Marine fishes and terrestrial amphibians are both ureotelic. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are false, so every other option fails.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every excretory structure works mainly in nitrogen removal.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human excretory system and urine formation
questions.question: The human kidneys are located between which vertebrae?
options: Last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae
First thoracic and third thoracic vertebrae
Third lumbar and first sacral vertebrae
Last cervical and first thoracic vertebrae

solution.key_concept: Position of the kidneys
steps: The kidneys are bean-shaped.
They lie between the last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Last thoracic and third lumbar vertebrae
solution.why_not_others: Options (2) and (4) place the kidneys too high. Option (3) places them too low.
solution.common_trap: Placing the kidneys entirely within the lumbar region.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human excretory system and urine formation
questions.question: The normal glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of a healthy human is approximately:

solution.key_concept: Glomerular filtration rate
steps: GFR is about 125 mL/min.
Converting to a daily figure: 125 mL × 1440 min = 180,000 mL, or about 180 L per day.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): 125 mL per minute
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) applies the daily number 180 to a per-minute unit. Option (3) is the daily urine output. Option (4) applies the per-minute number 125 to a per-day unit.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the GFR units with the urine output figures.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human excretory system and urine formation
questions.question: Which part of the nephron is impermeable to water but transports electrolytes?

solution.key_concept: Permeability of the two limbs of Henle's loop
steps: The descending limb is permeable to water.
The ascending limb is impermeable to water but transports electrolytes.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Ascending limb of Henle's loop
solution.why_not_others: The descending limb is permeable to water. The PCT reabsorbs 70 to 80% of the water. The collecting duct reabsorbs much water to concentrate urine.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the two limbs of Henle's loop.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human excretory system and urine formation
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Extensions of the cortex between the medullary pyramids

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Notch through which the ureter, blood vessels and nerves enter or leave

solution.key_concept: Structures of the kidney and the nephron
steps: The hilum is the notch for the ureter, blood vessels and nerves (A-II).
The columns of Bertini are cortical extensions between the pyramids (B-I).
The Malpighian body is the glomerulus plus Bowman's capsule (C-IV), and the PCT has cuboidal brush-border epithelium (D-III).
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps the hilum and the columns of Bertini. Option (2) swaps the Malpighian body and the PCT. Option (4) swaps the hilum and the Malpighian body.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the columns of Bertini with the medullary pyramids.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human excretory system and urine formation
questions.question: Which of the following statements about urine formation are correct?

statements.A: The medullary osmolarity gradient ranges from 300 to 1200 mOsmol per L and is maintained by NaCl and urea.
statements.B: Urine can become nearly ten times as concentrated as the initial filtrate.
statements.C: The PCT secretes $H^+$, $NH_3$ and $K^+$, helping to maintain pH.
statements.D: Cortical nephrons have long loops of Henle that dip deep into the medulla.
statements.E: Daily urine output is 1 to 1.5 L, containing 25 to 30 g of urea.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Concentration of urine and functions of the nephron
steps: A is true.
B is false: urine becomes nearly four times as concentrated as the filtrate.
C is true.
D is false: cortical nephrons have short loops, while juxtamedullary nephrons have long ones.
E is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) includes the false statement B. Option (2) includes the false statement D and omits A. Option (3) includes the false statement D.
solution.common_trap: Attributing the long loops of juxtamedullary nephrons to cortical nephrons.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting B and D leaves only option (4).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Osmoregulation and regulation of kidney function: renin-angiotensin, ANF, ADH, diabetes insipidus
questions.question: Antidiuretic hormone (vasopressin) is synthesised in which of the following?

solution.key_concept: ADH is made in the hypothalamus and released from the neurohypophysis (posterior pituitary).
steps: ADH is produced by hypothalamic neurosecretory cells.
It is stored in, and released from, the posterior pituitary.
So the site of synthesis is the hypothalamus.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Hypothalamus
solution.why_not_others: The posterior pituitary only stores and releases ADH. The adrenal cortex releases aldosterone. JG cells release renin.
solution.common_trap: Taking the site of release (posterior pituitary) to be the site of synthesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Osmoregulation and regulation of kidney function: renin-angiotensin, ANF, ADH, diabetes insipidus
questions.question: A fall in glomerular blood pressure first triggers the release of which substance, and from which source?

solution.key_concept: A fall in GFR or blood pressure activates the JG cells, which starts RAAS.
steps: The JGA senses the fall in GFR or blood pressure.
The JG cells release renin.
Renin converts angiotensinogen into angiotensin I, which is then converted into angiotensin II.
Aldosterone is released only later, when angiotensin II stimulates the adrenal cortex.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Renin from the juxtaglomerular cells
solution.why_not_others: ADH release is triggered by fluid loss sensed by osmoreceptors. ANF is released when blood flow to the atria increases. Aldosterone is a downstream step of RAAS, not the first response.
solution.common_trap: Choosing aldosterone because it is the best-known RAAS hormone, even though it acts later in the pathway.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Osmoregulation and regulation of kidney function: renin-angiotensin, ANF, ADH, diabetes insipidus
questions.question: A patient passes very large volumes of dilute urine, shows signs of dehydration and has normal blood glucose. The most likely cause is
options: Deficient insulin secretion from the pancreas
Excess ADH release from the neurohypophysis
Defective synthesis or release of ADH
Excess aldosterone secretion from the adrenal cortex

solution.key_concept: Diabetes insipidus is caused by defective ADH synthesis or release and leads to large volumes of dilute urine.
steps: Normal blood glucose rules out an insulin problem.
Without enough ADH, water is not reabsorbed from the DCT and collecting duct.
The result is copious dilute urine and dehydration, which is diabetes insipidus.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Defective synthesis or release of ADH
solution.why_not_others: An insulin problem causes hyperglycemia. Excess ADH increases water reabsorption and reduces urine volume. Excess aldosterone increases $Na^+$ and water reabsorption.
solution.common_trap: Confusing diabetes insipidus (ADH deficiency) with diabetes mellitus (an insulin problem).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Osmoregulation and regulation of kidney function: renin-angiotensin, ANF, ADH, diabetes insipidus
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Atrial natriuretic factor, released when blood flow to the atria increases, raises blood pressure by causing vasoconstriction.
statements.R: Atrial natriuretic factor acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: ANF causes vasodilation and lowers blood pressure, so it opposes RAAS.
steps: ANF is released when blood flow to the atria increases.
ANF causes vasodilation and decreases blood pressure, so A is false.
Because it opposes RAAS, ANF acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so any option that treats A as true is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Assigning the vasoconstrictor action of angiotensin II to ANF.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Osmoregulation and regulation of kidney function: renin-angiotensin, ANF, ADH, diabetes insipidus
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: An increase in body fluid volume stimulates the osmoreceptors, which then enhance ADH release from the neurohypophysis.
statements.II: Angiotensin II, besides being a powerful vasoconstrictor, stimulates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone, which promotes reabsorption of $Na^+$ and water from distal parts of the tubule.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Increased body fluid volume suppresses ADH release, while angiotensin II stimulates aldosterone release.
steps: An increase in body fluid volume switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses ADH release, so Statement I is incorrect.
Angiotensin II constricts blood vessels and stimulates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone.
Aldosterone causes $Na^+$ and water reabsorption from distal tubule parts, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution.why_not_others: Statement I reverses the feedback relationship, so options (1) and (3) fail. Statement II is accurate, so option (2) fails.
solution.common_trap: Assuming more fluid means more ADH, when in fact ADH is released in response to fluid loss.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Role of other organs in excretion
questions.question: Approximately how much carbon dioxide is removed by the human lungs per minute?

solution.key_concept: The lungs are a major excretory organ for $CO_2$.
steps: The lungs remove large amounts of $CO_2$, along with significant quantities of water.
The amount removed is about 200 mL per minute.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): 200 mL
solution.why_not_others: 20 mL and 2000 mL are ten-fold errors in either direction. 500 mL is an arbitrary value.
solution.common_trap: Making an order-of-magnitude slip with the figure.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Role of other organs in excretion
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the bile secreted by the liver?

solution.key_concept: Bile contains bilirubin, biliverdin, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins and drugs.
steps: List the components of bile: bile pigments, cholesterol, degraded steroid hormones, vitamins and drugs.
Waxes are eliminated through sebum from the sebaceous glands, not through bile.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Waxes
solution.why_not_others: Bilirubin, degraded steroid hormones and cholesterol are all excreted in bile.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the excretory products of the sebaceous glands with those of the liver.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Role of other organs in excretion
questions.question: What is the primary function of sweat secreted by the sweat glands?
options: To act as the main route of urea excretion
To form a protective oily covering on the skin

solution.key_concept: Sweat contains NaCl, small amounts of urea and lactic acid, but its main role is cooling.
steps: Sweat removes only small amounts of urea, so excretion is not its main role.
The primary function of sweat is to cool the body.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): To cool the body
solution.why_not_others: Urea in sweat is minor. The oily covering and the removal of sterols and hydrocarbons are functions of sebum.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that sweat is mainly excretory because it contains urea.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Role of other organs in excretion
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Each accessory excretory organ removes characteristic substances.
steps: Lungs remove $CO_2$ and water: A-II.
Liver excretes the bile pigments bilirubin and biliverdin: B-I.
Sebaceous glands release sterols, hydrocarbons and waxes in sebum: C-IV.
Sweat glands release NaCl, urea and lactic acid: D-III.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) swaps lungs and liver. Option (3) swaps sweat and sebum. Option (4) assigns sebum components to the liver.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the contents of sweat and sebum.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Role of other organs in excretion
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the role of other organs in excretion are correct?

statements.A: Saliva eliminates small amounts of nitrogenous wastes.
statements.B: Most substances present in bile leave the body along with digestive wastes.
statements.C: Sebum forms a protective oily covering on the skin.
statements.D: Sweat contains large amounts of urea, making the skin the main route of urea excretion.

solution.key_concept: Accessory excretory routes remove only specific or minor wastes.
steps: A is correct: saliva removes small amounts of nitrogenous waste.
B is correct: most bile constituents leave the body with digestive wastes.
C is correct: sebum forms a protective oily covering on the skin.
D is incorrect: sweat contains only small amounts of urea, and its main role is cooling.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, B and C only
solution.why_not_others: Options (2) and (4) include the false statement D. Option (1) leaves out the true statement C.
solution.common_trap: Overestimating how much urea is excreted through sweat.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Excretory disorders, dialysis and artificial kidney
questions.question: Accumulation of urea in the blood due to kidney malfunction is called

solution.key_concept: Uremia means excess urea in the blood.
steps: When the kidneys malfunction, urea accumulates in the blood.
This condition is called uremia, and it may lead to kidney failure.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Uremia
solution.why_not_others: Glomerulonephritis is inflammation of the glomeruli. Renal calculi are kidney stones. Diabetes insipidus is due to ADH deficiency.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the names of different kidney disorders.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Excretory disorders, dialysis and artificial kidney
questions.question: In haemodialysis, the dialysing fluid surrounding the cellophane tube has
options: The composition of plasma with added nitrogenous wastes
The same composition as plasma except for nitrogenous wastes

solution.key_concept: Dialysing fluid matches plasma minus the nitrogenous wastes, which creates a gradient for those wastes only.
steps: Nitrogenous wastes are absent from the dialysing fluid.
They therefore diffuse out of the blood down their concentration gradient.
All other plasma constituents are present at equal levels, so they are not lost.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): The same composition as plasma except for nitrogenous wastes
solution.why_not_others: Urine-like fluid or fluid with added wastes would not remove urea. Distilled water would drain useful solutes from the blood.
solution.common_trap: Thinking any waste-free fluid, such as water, would serve as dialysing fluid.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Excretory disorders, dialysis and artificial kidney
questions.question: Which of the following gives the correct sequence of steps in haemodialysis?
options: Blood drained from artery, anti-heparin added, passed through dialysing unit, heparin added, returned through vein
Blood drained from artery, heparin added, passed through dialysing unit, anti-heparin added, returned through vein
Blood drained from vein, heparin added, passed through dialysing unit, anti-heparin added, returned through artery
Blood drained from artery, heparin added, anti-heparin added, passed through dialysing unit, returned through vein

solution.key_concept: Heparin is added before dialysis and anti-heparin after it; blood is taken from an artery and returned through a vein.
steps: Blood is drained from a convenient artery.
Heparin is added to prevent clotting.
The blood is pumped through the dialysing unit.
Anti-heparin is added, and the blood is returned through a vein.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Blood drained from artery, heparin added, passed through dialysing unit, anti-heparin added, returned through vein
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) reverses the heparin and anti-heparin steps. Option (3) reverses the artery and vein. Option (4) neutralises heparin before dialysis.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the order in which heparin and anti-heparin are added.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Excretory disorders, dialysis and artificial kidney
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In haemodialysis, nitrogenous wastes are actively pumped out of the blood into the dialysing fluid by the cellophane tube.
statements.R: The dialysing fluid lacks nitrogenous wastes, which creates a concentration gradient across the porous cellophane membrane.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Wastes leave the blood by diffusion down a concentration gradient, not by active pumping.
steps: The dialysing fluid has no nitrogenous wastes, so a concentration gradient exists, which makes R true.
Wastes diffuse passively through the porous membrane.
The membrane does not actively pump wastes, so A is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so any option that treats A as true is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the machine pump that moves blood with active transport of wastes across the membrane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Excretory disorders, dialysis and artificial kidney
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Glomerulonephritis refers to the formation of insoluble masses of crystallised salts such as oxalates within the kidney.
statements.II: For kidney transplantation, a donor unrelated to the patient is preferred in order to minimise immune rejection.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Renal calculi and glomerulonephritis are different disorders, and a donor who is a close relative is preferred for transplantation.
steps: Crystallised salt masses such as oxalates are renal calculi; glomerulonephritis is inflammation of the glomeruli. So Statement I is incorrect.
A donor who is a close relative is preferred to minimise rejection, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Both statements contain errors, so any option that calls one of them correct is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the definitions of renal calculi and glomerulonephritis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Types of movement: ciliary, flagellar and muscular
questions.question: The swimming of human spermatozoa is an example of

solution.key_concept: Sperm motility is due to the whip-like beating of the flagellum.
steps: Spermatozoa have a flagellum.
Its whip-like beating drives the sperm forward, which is flagellar movement.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Flagellar movement
solution.why_not_others: Amoeboid movement is seen in leucocytes and macrophages. Ciliary movement is seen in tubular organs such as the trachea. Muscular movement moves the limbs, jaws and tongue.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the cilia-driven movement of ova with the movement of sperm.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Types of movement: ciliary, flagellar and muscular
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of process and type of movement is correctly matched?
options: Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract – ciliary movement
Water current in the canal system of sponges – amoeboid movement

solution.key_concept: Ciliary movement occurs in organs lined by ciliated epithelium, such as the female reproductive tract and the trachea.
steps: Cilia in the female reproductive tract help ova pass along it, so this pair is correct.
Macrophages show amoeboid movement.
Both the sponge canal current and Euglena locomotion are flagellar.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Passage of ova through the female reproductive tract – ciliary movement
solution.why_not_others: Macrophages are amoeboid, not ciliary. The sponge water current and Euglena both depend on flagella.
solution.common_trap: Calling the sponge water current ciliary when it is driven by flagella.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Types of movement: ciliary, flagellar and muscular
questions.question: Muscles make up approximately what percentage of the body weight of a human adult?

solution.key_concept: Muscle is mesodermal tissue and forms a large share of adult body weight.
steps: Muscle tissue makes up about 40 to 50% of adult body weight.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): 40 to 50%
solution.why_not_others: The other ranges either underestimate or overestimate the proportion of muscle.
solution.common_trap: Underestimating the proportion of muscle in body weight.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Types of movement: ciliary, flagellar and muscular
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_I.label: B
list_I.text: Removal of dust from the trachea

solution.key_concept: Each type of movement occurs in specific cells or organs.
steps: Leucocytes move by pseudopodia: A-II.
Cilia lining the trachea clear inhaled dust: B-IV.
Sperm swim using a flagellum: C-III.
Limbs and jaws are moved by muscles: D-I.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps amoeboid and ciliary movement. Option (3) swaps ciliary and flagellar movement. Option (4) swaps amoeboid and muscular movement.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging ciliary and flagellar movement.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Types of movement: ciliary, flagellar and muscular
questions.question: Which of the following statements about movement and muscles are correct?

statements.A: Microfilaments are involved in amoeboid movement.
statements.B: Visceral muscle is striated and involuntary.
statements.C: Muscles show excitability, contractility, extensibility and elasticity.
statements.E: Locomotion requires coordinated activity of the muscular, skeletal and neural systems.

solution.key_concept: Know the basis of amoeboid movement, the properties and origin of muscle, and what locomotion requires.
steps: A is correct: microfilaments are involved in amoeboid movement.
B is incorrect: visceral muscle is smooth (non-striated) and involuntary.
C is correct: these are the four properties of muscle.
D is incorrect: muscle is mesodermal in origin.
E is correct: locomotion needs coordinated activity of the muscular, skeletal and neural systems.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options (1) and (2) include the false statements B or D. Option (3) leaves out the true statement C.
solution.common_trap: Calling visceral muscle striated, or treating muscle as ectodermal.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle: contractile proteins and muscle contraction
questions.question: The functional unit of contraction in a skeletal muscle fibre is the

solution.key_concept: The sarcomere is the segment of a myofibril between two successive Z lines. It is the functional unit of contraction.
steps: A myofibril is made of repeating units that are each bounded by two Z lines.
Each such unit is a sarcomere, and it is the sarcomere that shortens during contraction.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Sarcomere
solution.why_not_others: A myofibril is a chain of many sarcomeres. A fascicle is a bundle of muscle fibres. A motor unit is one motor neuron together with the muscle fibres it supplies.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the motor unit, which is a functional neuromuscular grouping, with the sarcomere, which is the contractile unit.
solution.time_saving_tip: Link the phrase 'between two Z lines' with the word sarcomere.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle: contractile proteins and muscle contraction
questions.question: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, which of the following keeps its length unchanged?

solution.key_concept: In the sliding filament theory, thin filaments slide over thick filaments. The filaments themselves do not shorten.
steps: Myosin heads pull the actin filaments towards the centre of the A band.
This sliding brings the Z lines closer together, so the sarcomere shortens.
The I band and the H zone narrow.
The A band corresponds to the length of the myosin filaments, so it stays the same length.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A band
solution.why_not_others: The I band, the H zone and the whole sarcomere all shorten during contraction.
solution.common_trap: Believing the A band shortens because the whole sarcomere shortens.
solution.time_saving_tip: A band = myosin length, so the A band is constant.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle: contractile proteins and muscle contraction
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the head of a myosin monomer?
options: It forms the tail portion called light meromyosin
It masks the myosin-binding sites on actin in a resting muscle
It binds the $Ca^{2+}$ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
It acts as an ATPase and has active sites for both ATP and actin
