solution.key_concept: Each myosin monomer (meromyosin) has a head with a short arm (HMM) and a tail (LMM). The head acts as an ATPase.
steps: The head and short arm together form heavy meromyosin, and the tail is light meromyosin.
The head hydrolyses ATP, so it acts as an ATPase.
The head has active sites for ATP and for actin, which allows cross-bridge formation.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): It acts as an ATPase and has active sites for both ATP and actin
solution.why_not_others: Light meromyosin is the tail, not the head. Troponin masks the binding sites at rest. Troponin, not myosin, binds $Ca^{2+}$.
solution.common_trap: Attributing the roles of troponin to myosin.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle: contractile proteins and muscle contraction
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: During contraction of skeletal muscle, the I bands get reduced in width.
statements.R: During contraction, the myosin filaments themselves shorten and pull the Z lines closer together.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: In the sliding filament mechanism, the filaments slide past each other but do not shorten.
steps: Thin filaments slide towards the centre of the A band, so the I bands narrow. A is true.
The myosin filaments do not shorten, which is why the A band length stays constant. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options (1) and (2) are ruled out. A is true, so option (4) is ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that filament shortening, rather than filament sliding, causes contraction.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal muscle: contractile proteins and muscle contraction
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Binding of a fresh ATP molecule to the myosin head breaks the cross bridge between actin and myosin.
statements.II: $Ca^{2+}$ ions bind to tropomyosin, which then unmasks the myosin-binding sites on actin.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: $Ca^{2+}$ binds troponin to expose the binding sites on actin. Fresh ATP releases myosin from actin.
steps: After the power stroke, a new ATP binds the myosin head and the cross bridge breaks. Statement I is correct.
$Ca^{2+}$ binds troponin, not tropomyosin. Tropomyosin only runs along the actin filament. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II assigns the calcium-binding role to the wrong protein, so any option calling it correct fails. Statement I is correct, so the options calling it incorrect also fail.
solution.common_trap: Swapping troponin and tropomyosin.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember: Troponin catches Calcium.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal system and joints
questions.question: The number of bones in the axial skeleton of an adult human is

solution.key_concept: $206 = 80_{axial} + 126_{appendicular}$
steps: The axial skeleton includes the skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs.
Together these account for 80 bones.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): 80
solution.why_not_others: 126 is the appendicular count, 206 is the total and 22 is the number of skull bones.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the axial and appendicular counts.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal system and joints
questions.question: Which of the following joint–example pairs is correctly matched?
options: Pivot joint – between atlas and axis
Gliding joint – between carpal and metacarpal of the thumb

solution.key_concept: Synovial joints are of several types, each with a characteristic example.
steps: Atlas and axis form a pivot joint.
The knee is a hinge joint.
The joint between carpals is a gliding joint.
The joint between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb is a saddle joint.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Pivot joint – between atlas and axis
solution.why_not_others: Options (2), (3) and (4) attach a joint type to an example that belongs to a different type.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the gliding and saddle joints of the hand.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal system and joints
questions.question: Of the 12 pairs of ribs in humans, how many pairs are neither true ribs nor floating ribs?

solution.key_concept: There are 7 pairs of true ribs, 3 pairs of vertebrochondral ribs and 2 pairs of floating ribs.
steps: Subtract the true and floating ribs from the total: $12 - 7 - 2 = 3$.
These 3 pairs are the vertebrochondral ribs.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): 3
solution.why_not_others: 2 is the number of floating rib pairs and 7 is the number of true rib pairs. 5 comes from subtracting only the true ribs from the total.
solution.common_trap: Subtracting only one of the two categories.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal system and joints
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Forms the shoulder joint with the humerus

solution.key_concept: Each landmark of the girdles and skull has a specific articulation or feature.
steps: The glenoid cavity of the scapula forms the shoulder joint with the humerus: A-III.
The acetabulum receives the femur: B-II.
The pubic symphysis contains fibrous cartilage: C-IV.
The occipital condyles articulate with the atlas: D-I.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps the shoulder and hip sockets. Option (3) swaps the pubic symphysis with the occipital condyles. Option (4) misplaces the glenoid cavity and the pubic symphysis.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the glenoid cavity (shoulder) and the acetabulum (hip).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Skeletal system and joints
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the human skeleton are correct?

statements.A: The skull is dicondylic, joining the vertebral column through two occipital condyles.
statements.B: The vertebral column has 26 vertebrae, of which 12 are lumbar.
statements.C: Each forelimb has 8 carpals and 14 phalanges.
statements.D: Cartilaginous joints, such as the skull sutures, allow no movement.
statements.E: Each coxal bone is formed by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: The vertebral formula is $26 = 7 + 12 + 5 + 1 + 1$. Skull sutures are fibrous joints.
steps: A is correct: the skull joins the vertebral column through two occipital condyles.
B is wrong: there are 5 lumbar vertebrae, while 12 is the thoracic count.
C is correct: each forelimb has 8 carpals and 14 phalanges.
D is wrong: skull sutures are fibrous joints, and cartilaginous joints allow limited movement.
E is correct: each coxal bone forms by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options (1), (2) and (4) each include B or D, which are false.
solution.common_trap: Assigning the 12 thoracic vertebrae to the lumbar region, and calling sutures cartilaginous.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Muscular and skeletal disorders: myasthenia gravis, tetany, muscular dystrophy, arthritis, osteoporosis, gout
questions.question: Gout is caused by
options: an autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction
accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints

solution.key_concept: Gout is inflammation of the joints caused by deposition of uric acid crystals.
steps: Identify the specific cause of gout: deposition of uric acid crystals in the joints.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
solution.why_not_others: Low $Ca^{2+}$ causes tetany, low estrogen is linked to osteoporosis, and an autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction is myasthenia gravis.
solution.common_trap: Attributing uric acid to arthritis in general rather than specifically to gout.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Muscular and skeletal disorders: myasthenia gravis, tetany, muscular dystrophy, arthritis, osteoporosis, gout
questions.question: An autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction that causes fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle is

solution.key_concept: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction.
steps: Note the key words 'autoimmune' and 'neuromuscular junction'.
These key words point to myasthenia gravis.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Myasthenia gravis
solution.why_not_others: Muscular dystrophy is genetic, tetany is due to low $Ca^{2+}$, and osteoporosis is a bone disorder.
solution.common_trap: Confusing myasthenia gravis with muscular dystrophy because both weaken muscle.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Muscular and skeletal disorders: myasthenia gravis, tetany, muscular dystrophy, arthritis, osteoporosis, gout
questions.question: Which of the following disorder–cause pairs is incorrectly matched?
options: Gout – uric acid crystals in joints

solution.key_concept: Tetany results from low, not high, $Ca^{2+}$ in body fluids.
steps: Check each pair against its known cause.
Tetany is caused by low $Ca^{2+}$, so this pair is wrong.
The other three pairs are correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Tetany – high $Ca^{2+}$ in body fluids
solution.why_not_others: Osteoporosis is linked to low estrogen, muscular dystrophy is mostly genetic, and gout is due to uric acid crystals.
solution.common_trap: Linking tetany to excess calcium.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Muscular and skeletal disorders: myasthenia gravis, tetany, muscular dystrophy, arthritis, osteoporosis, gout
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Osteoporosis is associated with an increased chance of bone fractures.
statements.R: Arthritis is inflammation of the joints.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Osteoporosis raises fracture risk through decreased bone mass, not through joint inflammation.
steps: A is true: osteoporosis reduces bone mass and raises fracture risk.
R is true: arthritis is inflammation of the joints.
Joint inflammation does not explain fragile bones, so R does not explain A.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, so options (3) and (4) fail. R does not explain A, so option (1) fails.
solution.common_trap: Treating any two bone or joint facts as cause and effect.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Muscular and skeletal disorders: myasthenia gravis, tetany, muscular dystrophy, arthritis, osteoporosis, gout
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Tetany is characterised by rapid spasms of muscle due to low $Ca^{2+}$ in body fluids.
statements.II: Myasthenia gravis is a genetic disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Myasthenia gravis is autoimmune, whereas muscular dystrophy is genetic and progressive.
steps: Statement I correctly describes tetany.
Statement II describes muscular dystrophy, not myasthenia gravis, which is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement I is correct, so options (2) and (4) fail. Statement II is incorrect, so option (1) fails.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging myasthenia gravis and muscular dystrophy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Neuron and nerves
questions.question: Bipolar neurons, having one axon and one dendrite, are found in the

solution.key_concept: Neurons are classified by structure, and each type occurs in a characteristic location.
steps: Bipolar neurons have one axon and one dendrite.
Bipolar neurons occur in the retina.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Retina
solution.why_not_others: Multipolar neurons occur in the cerebral cortex and unipolar neurons in the embryonic stage. Synaptic knobs are axon terminals, not a location for a neuron type.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the locations of bipolar and multipolar neurons.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Neuron and nerves
questions.question: Nissl's granules are present in which parts of a neuron?

solution.key_concept: Nissl's granules occur in the cell body and dendrites but are absent from the axon.
steps: The cell body contains Nissl's granules.
Dendrites also contain Nissl's granules.
The axon lacks Nissl's granules.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Cell body and dendrites only
solution.why_not_others: Every other option includes the axon, which lacks Nissl's granules.
solution.common_trap: Assuming Nissl's granules occur throughout the neuron.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Neuron and nerves
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Neuron types and fibre types each occur in characteristic locations.
steps: Multipolar neurons occur in the cerebral cortex: A-III.
Bipolar neurons occur in the retina: B-I.
Unipolar neurons occur in the embryonic stage: C-IV.
Myelinated fibres occur in spinal and cranial nerves: D-II.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) swaps the multipolar and bipolar locations. Option (3) swaps unipolar neurons with myelinated fibres. Option (4) swaps the multipolar and unipolar locations.
solution.common_trap: Placing bipolar neurons in the cortex.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Neuron and nerves
questions.question: Which of the following statements about neurons are correct?

statements.A: Dendrites carry impulses towards the cell body.
statements.B: Synaptic knobs at the axon terminals contain synaptic vesicles filled with neurotransmitters.
statements.C: Unipolar neurons have one axon and one dendrite.
statements.D: Unmyelinated fibres are not associated with Schwann cells at all.
statements.E: The neuron is the structural and functional unit of the neural system.

options: A, B, C and E only

solution.key_concept: Check each statement against the structure and classification of neurons.
steps: A is correct: dendrites conduct impulses towards the cell body.
B is correct: synaptic knobs contain vesicles filled with neurotransmitters.
C is wrong: unipolar neurons have a cell body and one axon only, whereas one axon with one dendrite describes a bipolar neuron.
D is wrong: unmyelinated fibres are enclosed by Schwann cells, just without a myelin sheath.
E is correct: the neuron is the structural and functional unit.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A, B and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options (2), (3) and (4) each include C or D, which are false.
solution.common_trap: Assuming unmyelinated fibres have no Schwann cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human nervous system: central, peripheral and visceral
questions.question: Which of the following groups of brain regions together form the brain stem in humans?

solution.key_concept: Divisions of the human brain and composition of the brain stem
steps: The forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus.
The hindbrain consists of the pons, cerebellum and medulla.
The midbrain, pons and medulla together form the brain stem.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Midbrain, pons and medulla
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 lists the forebrain. Option 2 lists the hindbrain, which includes the cerebellum but not the midbrain. Option 4 includes the thalamus, which is a forebrain structure.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the hindbrain with the brain stem. The cerebellum is part of the hindbrain but not of the brain stem.
solution.time_saving_tip: Any option containing the cerebellum or a forebrain part can be eliminated at once.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human nervous system: central, peripheral and visceral
questions.question: A region of the human brain contains the centres that control respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretion. This region is the

solution.key_concept: Functions of the hindbrain regions
steps: The medulla houses the centres for respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretion.
The medulla is part of both the hindbrain and the brain stem.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Medulla
solution.why_not_others: The cerebellum is highly convoluted to accommodate more neurons and is not the site of these centres. The hypothalamus controls body temperature, eating and drinking. The thalamus is the major coordinating centre for sensory and motor signalling.
solution.common_trap: Choosing the hypothalamus because it regulates many body functions such as temperature and thirst.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human nervous system: central, peripheral and visceral
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the autonomic neural system of humans?
options: It is a part of the central neural system that supplies skeletal muscles
It is a division of the peripheral neural system that supplies involuntary organs and smooth muscles and has sympathetic and parasympathetic parts
It consists only of afferent fibres that carry impulses from organs to the CNS
It is a division of the peripheral neural system that supplies skeletal muscles and has sympathetic and parasympathetic parts

solution.key_concept: Divisions of the peripheral neural system
steps: The PNS has two divisions: somatic and autonomic.
The somatic division supplies skeletal muscles.
The autonomic division supplies involuntary organs and smooth muscles.
The autonomic division is further divided into sympathetic and parasympathetic parts.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): It is a division of the peripheral neural system that supplies involuntary organs and smooth muscles and has sympathetic and parasympathetic parts
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 is wrong because the autonomic system is part of the PNS, not the CNS, and skeletal muscles are supplied by the somatic division. Option 3 is wrong because afferent fibres are a feature of PNS nerves in general, not a definition of the autonomic system. Option 4 wrongly assigns skeletal muscles to the autonomic division.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the targets of the somatic and autonomic divisions.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human nervous system: central, peripheral and visceral
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: The hypothalamus is a part of the hindbrain in humans.
statements.R: The hindbrain consists of the pons, cerebellum and medulla.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Components of the forebrain and hindbrain
steps: The forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus, so A is false.
The hindbrain consists of the pons, cerebellum and medulla, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 3 all require A to be true, but the hypothalamus belongs to the forebrain.
solution.common_trap: Placing the hypothalamus in the hindbrain because, like the medulla, it controls vital functions.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human nervous system: central, peripheral and visceral
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In the cerebrum, the cerebral cortex forms the white matter while the inner tracts form the grey matter.
statements.II: The corpora quadrigemina and the cerebral aqueduct are structures of the hindbrain.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Grey and white matter of the cerebrum; structures of the midbrain
steps: The cerebral cortex is grey matter and the inner tracts form white matter, so Statement I reverses them and is incorrect.
The corpora quadrigemina and the cerebral aqueduct belong to the midbrain, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each of the other options treats at least one statement as correct, but both statements contain a factual reversal.
solution.common_trap: Reversing grey and white matter, and assigning midbrain structures to the hindbrain.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Generation and conduction of nerve impulse
questions.question: Depolarisation of the axonal membrane during generation of a nerve impulse is caused by

solution.key_concept: Ionic basis of the action potential
steps: A stimulus makes the membrane freely permeable to $Na^+$.
Rapid influx of $Na^+$ reverses the polarity of the membrane; this reversal is depolarisation.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Rapid influx of $Na^+$
solution.why_not_others: Efflux of $K^+$ causes repolarisation, not depolarisation. Influx of $K^+$ and efflux of $Na^+$ describe the action of the sodium-potassium pump, which maintains the resting gradients.
solution.common_trap: Confusing depolarisation ($Na^+$ influx) with repolarisation ($K^+$ efflux).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Generation and conduction of nerve impulse
questions.question: In an axonal membrane, sodium-potassium pumps expel 3600 $Na^+$ ions. How many $K^+$ ions are moved into the axoplasm during this activity?

solution.key_concept: Stoichiometry of the sodium-potassium pump
steps: The pump moves 3 $Na^+$ out for every 2 $K^+$ moved in.
$K^+$ moved in $= 3600 \times \frac{2}{3} = 2400$.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): 2400
solution.why_not_others: 5400 results from inverting the ratio ($3600 \times 3/2$). 3600 assumes a 1:1 exchange. 1800 simply halves the number of $Na^+$ ions.
solution.common_trap: Inverting the 3:2 ratio of the pump.
solution.time_saving_tip: For every 3 $Na^+$ out, 2 $K^+$ come in, so the $K^+$ number must be smaller than the $Na^+$ number but more than half of it.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Generation and conduction of nerve impulse
questions.question: Which of the following is correct for the axonal membrane of a neuron at rest?
options: It is more permeable to $Na^+$ than to $K^+$
It is impermeable to the negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm
Its inner surface is positively charged with respect to its outer surface
The axoplasm inside it contains a high concentration of $Na^+$ and a low concentration of $K^+$

solution.key_concept: Basis of the resting potential
steps: At rest the membrane is more permeable to $K^+$, nearly impermeable to $Na^+$, and impermeable to the negative proteins of the axoplasm.
The axoplasm is high in $K^+$ and low in $Na^+$.
As a result, the outer surface is positive and the inner surface is negative.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): It is impermeable to the negatively charged proteins present in the axoplasm
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 reverses the relative permeabilities. Option 3 reverses the polarity. Option 4 reverses the ion distribution.
solution.common_trap: Reversing which side of the resting membrane is positive.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Generation and conduction of nerve impulse
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Diffusion of $K^+$ out of the axon

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Rapid influx of $Na^+$ reversing membrane polarity

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Pre- and post-synaptic membranes in very close contact

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Outer surface positive and inner surface negative

solution.key_concept: Events of nerve impulse generation and types of synapse
steps: Resting potential: the outer surface is positive and the inner surface negative (A-IV).
Depolarisation: rapid $Na^+$ influx reverses polarity (B-II).
Repolarisation: $K^+$ diffuses out and restores the resting state (C-I).
Electrical synapse: the membranes are in very close contact (D-III).
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 confuses the resting state with depolarisation. Option 2 swaps the ions responsible for depolarisation and repolarisation. Option 4 swaps repolarisation with the electrical synapse.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the roles of $Na^+$ and $K^+$ in depolarisation and repolarisation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Generation and conduction of nerve impulse
questions.question: Which of the following statements about synaptic transmission are correct?

statements.A: Impulse transmission across an electrical synapse is faster than across a chemical synapse.
statements.B: Electrical synapses are more common than chemical synapses in the human neural system.
statements.C: At a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters cross the synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on the post-synaptic membrane.
statements.D: The new potential developed in the post-synaptic neuron is always excitatory.
statements.E: Binding of neurotransmitters opens ion channels on the post-synaptic membrane.

solution.key_concept: Electrical and chemical synapses
steps: A is correct: electrical transmission is faster.
B is incorrect: electrical synapses are rare.
C is correct: neurotransmitters cross the cleft and bind post-synaptic receptors.
D is incorrect: the new potential can be excitatory or inhibitory.
E is correct: neurotransmitter binding opens ion channels.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 3 each include either B (electrical synapses are rare) or D (the potential may be inhibitory), both of which are false.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that every synaptic signal excites the next neuron.
solution.time_saving_tip: Eliminating B and D removes every option except (4).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endocrine glands and hormones: hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads
questions.question: Melatonin, the hormone that regulates diurnal rhythms of the body, is secreted by the

solution.key_concept: Hormone of the pineal gland
steps: The pineal gland secretes melatonin.
Melatonin regulates diurnal (24-hour) rhythms.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Pineal gland
solution.why_not_others: The pituitary secretes GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH and MSH. The thyroid secretes $T_4$, $T_3$ and thyrocalcitonin. The adrenal medulla secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline.
solution.common_trap: Confusing melatonin with MSH from the pars intermedia because the names sound alike.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endocrine glands and hormones: hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is secreted by the pars intermedia of the human pituitary?

solution.key_concept: Parts of the adenohypophysis and their secretions
steps: The adenohypophysis consists of the pars distalis and the pars intermedia.
The pars distalis secretes GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
The pars intermedia secretes MSH.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): MSH
solution.why_not_others: Prolactin and ACTH come from the pars distalis. Oxytocin is made in the hypothalamus and released by the neurohypophysis.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that every anterior pituitary hormone comes from the pars distalis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endocrine glands and hormones: hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads
questions.question: The outermost layer of the human adrenal cortex is the

solution.key_concept: Layers of the adrenal cortex
steps: The adrenal cortex has three layers.
From outside to inside, they are the zona glomerulosa, the zona fasciculata and the zona reticularis.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Zona glomerulosa
solution.why_not_others: The zona fasciculata is the middle layer and the zona reticularis is the inner layer. The adrenal medulla is not a layer of the cortex at all.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the order of the cortical layers.
solution.time_saving_tip: Mnemonic GFR, from outside in: Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, Reticularis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endocrine glands and hormones: hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Glucagon is a hyperglycemic hormone.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Action of glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells
steps: Glucagon is secreted by the alpha cells of the pancreatic islets and is hyperglycemic, so A is true.
Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, so R is true.
These two processes raise blood glucose, so R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, which rules out options 3 and 4. R is the direct cause of A, which rules out option 2.
solution.common_trap: Confusing glucagon with insulin, which is hypoglycemic and promotes glycogenesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Endocrine glands and hormones: hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: LH causes ovulation and maintains the corpus luteum in females, while in males it stimulates the secretion of androgens.
statements.II: Oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesised in the hypothalamus and are stored and released by the neurohypophysis.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Functions of LH and the origin of posterior pituitary hormones
steps: LH stimulates androgen secretion in males, and causes ovulation and maintains the corpus luteum in females, so Statement I is correct.
Oxytocin and vasopressin are made in the hypothalamus; the neurohypophysis only stores and releases them, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Neither statement contains an error, so every option that marks a statement incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Believing that the posterior pituitary synthesises oxytocin and ADH, or attributing the functions of FSH to LH.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of hormone action; hormones as messengers and regulators
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is a steroid?

solution.key_concept: Chemical classification of hormones
steps: The steroid hormones include cortisol, testosterone, estradiol and progesterone.
Insulin and glucagon are peptide or protein hormones, and epinephrine is an amino-acid derivative.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Cortisol
solution.why_not_others: Insulin and glucagon are protein hormones. Epinephrine is an amino-acid derivative.
solution.common_trap: Treating epinephrine as a steroid because both it and cortisol come from the adrenal gland.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of hormone action; hormones as messengers and regulators
questions.question: Atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), a hormone produced by a non-endocrine tissue, is secreted by the

solution.key_concept: Hormones from non-endocrine tissues
steps: The heart secretes ANF.
The kidney secretes erythropoietin, and the GI tract secretes gastrin, secretin, CCK and GIP.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Heart
solution.why_not_others: The kidney secretes erythropoietin. The GI tract secretes gastrin, secretin, CCK and GIP. The adrenal cortex is an endocrine gland that secretes glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.
solution.common_trap: Linking ANF to the kidney because it affects salt balance.
solution.time_saving_tip: The word 'atrial' points to the heart.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of hormone action; hormones as messengers and regulators
questions.question: Which gastrointestinal hormone stimulates the release of water and bicarbonate ions from the exocrine pancreas?

solution.key_concept: Actions of GI tract hormones
steps: Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas to release water and bicarbonate.
CCK, by contrast, stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion and bile release.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Secretin
solution.why_not_others: Gastrin stimulates secretion of HCl and pepsinogen. CCK stimulates pancreatic enzymes and bile release. GIP inhibits gastric secretion and motility.
solution.common_trap: Confusing secretin (water and bicarbonate) with CCK (pancreatic enzymes and bile).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of hormone action; hormones as messengers and regulators
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Chemical nature of hormones
steps: Epinephrine is an amino-acid derivative (A-III).
Progesterone is a steroid (B-I).
Glucagon is a peptide/protein hormone (C-II).
Thyroxine is an iodothyronine (D-IV).
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps epinephrine and glucagon. Option 2 swaps progesterone and thyroxine. Option 4 swaps epinephrine and thyroxine.
solution.common_trap: Classifying thyroid hormones as steroids because both act on intracellular receptors.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Mechanism of hormone action; hormones as messengers and regulators
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the mechanism of hormone action are correct?

statements.A: Hormones that bind to membrane-bound receptors usually do not enter the target cell.
statements.B: cAMP, $IP_3$ and $Ca^{2+}$ act as second messengers.
statements.C: Steroid hormones are water-soluble and act through membrane-bound receptors.
statements.D: Thyroid hormones bind intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression.
statements.E: A single hormone receptor can bind many different hormones.

solution.key_concept: Membrane-bound and intracellular receptors; second messengers
steps: A is correct: hormones that bind membrane receptors usually do not enter the cell.
B is correct: cAMP, $IP_3$ and $Ca^{2+}$ are second messengers.
C is incorrect: steroids are lipid-soluble and act on intracellular receptors.
D is correct: thyroid hormones act on intracellular receptors and regulate gene expression.
E is incorrect: each receptor is specific to one hormone.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 includes C, option 2 includes E, and option 4 includes C; both C and E are false.
solution.common_trap: Assuming steroid hormones use second messengers the way protein hormones do.
solution.time_saving_tip: Eliminating C and E leaves only option (3).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Hormonal disorders: dwarfism, acromegaly, cretinism, goitre, exophthalmic goitre, diabetes, Addison's disease
questions.question: Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age, results in which of the following disorders?

solution.key_concept: The effect of a growth hormone (GH) imbalance depends on the age at which it occurs.
steps: Excess GH in childhood causes gigantism.
Low GH in childhood causes pituitary dwarfism.
Excess GH in adults, especially in middle age, causes acromegaly, with severe disfigurement, especially of the face.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Acromegaly
solution.why_not_others: Gigantism is due to excess GH in childhood, not adulthood. Pituitary dwarfism is due to GH deficiency in childhood. Cretinism is due to hypothyroidism in the developing baby, not to GH.
solution.common_trap: Confusing gigantism with acromegaly. Both are caused by excess GH, but they occur at different ages.
solution.time_saving_tip: Childhood excess means gigantism; adult excess means acromegaly.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Hormonal disorders: dwarfism, acromegaly, cretinism, goitre, exophthalmic goitre, diabetes, Addison's disease
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of a disorder and its cause is correctly matched?
options: Simple goitre - Iodine deficiency in the diet
Addison's disease - Overproduction of adrenal cortex hormones

solution.key_concept: Each endocrine disorder has a specific hormonal cause.
steps: Iodine deficiency in the diet causes hypothyroidism and thyroid enlargement, called simple goitre.
Diabetes insipidus is due to ADH deficiency.
Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism.
Addison's disease results from underproduction of adrenal cortex hormones.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Simple goitre - Iodine deficiency in the diet
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) is wrong because insulin is linked to diabetes mellitus, not diabetes insipidus. Option (3) is wrong because Graves' disease is hyperthyroidism. Option (4) is wrong because Addison's disease involves hypofunction of the adrenal cortex, not overproduction.
solution.common_trap: Linking diabetes insipidus to insulin because both conditions are called 'diabetes'.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Hormonal disorders: dwarfism, acromegaly, cretinism, goitre, exophthalmic goitre, diabetes, Addison's disease
questions.question: Which of the following features is NOT associated with cretinism?
options: Protruding eyeballs with increased BMR and weight loss

solution.key_concept: Cretinism results from hypothyroidism during pregnancy affecting the developing baby.
steps: Cretinism causes stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism.
Protruding eyeballs, increased BMR and weight loss are features of exophthalmic goitre, which is a form of hyperthyroidism.
Hyperthyroid features cannot belong to a hypothyroid disorder.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Protruding eyeballs with increased BMR and weight loss
solution.why_not_others: Stunted growth, deaf-mutism, mental retardation and low IQ are all listed features of cretinism.
solution.common_trap: Grouping all thyroid disorders together and missing that Graves' disease is hyperthyroid while cretinism is hypothyroid.
solution.time_saving_tip: Increased BMR points to hyperthyroidism, so it cannot fit cretinism.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Hormonal disorders: dwarfism, acromegaly, cretinism, goitre, exophthalmic goitre, diabetes, Addison's disease
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Iodine deficiency in the diet leads to enlargement of the thyroid gland.
statements.R: Hypothyroidism in adult women causes irregular menstrual cycles.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Iodine deficiency causes simple goitre, and hypothyroidism has separate effects in adult women.
steps: Assertion A is true: iodine deficiency causes hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid, called goitre.
Reason R is true: in adult women, hypothyroidism causes irregular menstrual cycles.
R describes another effect of hypothyroidism. It does not explain why the thyroid enlarges.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) is wrong because R does not explain thyroid enlargement. Options (3) and (4) are wrong because both statements are true.
solution.common_trap: Choosing option (1) just because both statements are about hypothyroidism.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Hormonal disorders: dwarfism, acromegaly, cretinism, goitre, exophthalmic goitre, diabetes, Addison's disease
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Excess secretion of growth hormone in childhood causes acromegaly, while its deficiency in childhood causes pituitary dwarfism.
statements.II: Diabetes insipidus is caused by insulin deficiency and is characterised by glycosuria and ketonuria.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Distinguish gigantism from acromegaly, and diabetes mellitus from diabetes insipidus.
steps: Excess GH in childhood causes gigantism. Acromegaly is due to excess GH in adults.
Statement I is therefore incorrect, even though its second half (dwarfism from low GH in childhood) is right.
Diabetes insipidus is due to ADH deficiency and causes water loss.
Glycosuria and ketonuria with insulin deficiency describe diabetes mellitus, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement I wrongly links childhood GH excess to acromegaly. Statement II wrongly gives diabetes insipidus the cause and features of diabetes mellitus. Since neither statement is correct, options (1), (3) and (4) are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Accepting Statement I because its second half is correct, and confusing the two types of diabetes.
solution.time_saving_tip: One wrong half makes the whole statement incorrect.
